about: What every hitop surface (CLI, MCP, hitop-core, the web app and desktop through hitop-wasm, HitopKit) does to a request when sending it or writing a snippet: send behaviour, not collection format (spec/collection-format.md is unchanged). Tested by hitop-core (tests/send_vectors.rs), webapp/tests/unit.mjs and HitopKit (SendRulesTests). Cases are only added. CC BY 4.0, like the specification.
whitespace: Leading and trailing whitespace is JavaScript's: U+0009-000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 and U+FEFF (not U+0085).

contentType.rules: A raw body of a POST, PUT or PATCH request (method compared without case) that has no Content-Type header with a value gets one, decided by the body after variables and the pre-request script: first character after leading whitespace '{' or '[' is application/json; '<html' or '<!doctype html' (ASCII case-insensitive, one space) is text/html; any other '<' is application/xml; anything else is text/plain; an empty or blank body gets none. Form and GraphQL bodies set their own. Never saved to the collection.

scheme.rules: The URL as sent, after variables and the pre-request script, leading and trailing whitespace removed. A URL with a scheme (letters, digits, + . -, then ':', unless it is host:port) is sent as it is. localhost, 127.x.x.x, 0.0.0.0 or [::1] (ASCII case-insensitive), with an optional :port and then nothing or / ? #, get http://. A host with a dot or a :port (ASCII letters, digits, _ and -), then optionally / ? # and no whitespace, gets https://. Anything else is an error: '"<url>" isn't a URL. Enter a full URL, such as https://api.example.com/users'.
